source.title: The Admiral's Sea
source.summary: From amir al-bahr to admiral: how Islamic naval power shaped the language of maritime command.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: Every navy in the world uses a title born from Arabic: admiral, from amir al-bahr, meaning "commander of the sea." Explore the 600-ship Fatimid navy, the Indian Ocean dhow trade, Zheng He's treasure fleets commanded by a Muslim admiral, and the tragic irony of how Islamic maritime knowledge enabled the very voyages that transformed global trade routes forever.

x.single_post: Every navy commander from Norfolk to Shanghai holds a title born in Arabic. Admiral comes from amir al-bahr, meaning commander of the sea. Why did Islamic maritime power leave such deep marks in languages across the world?
thread: Every navy commander from Norfolk to Shanghai holds a title born in Arabic. Admiral comes from amir al-bahr, meaning commander of the sea.
The Fatimid navy once commanded 600 ships across the Mediterranean. Islamic dhows carried trade from Zanzibar to Canton for centuries.
Zheng He's treasure fleets—seven massive expeditions that reached Africa—were commanded by a Muslim admiral named Wang Jinghong.
The irony cuts deep: Islamic maritime knowledge enabled the very European voyages that would reshape global trade routes forever. Listen: https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-tt-3
